claims.text: A framework combining DFT and on-the-fly machine learning can separately calculate lattice and electronic heat transport.
The proposed framework will be more accurate for HfNbTaTiZr than existing models that conflate lattice and electronic contributions.
Below 200 K, the predicted lattice thermal conductivity will be approximately 15–20% lower than predictions from earlier conflated models.
For HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen, the predicted total thermal conductivity from 300 to 1200 K will be 10–17 W/(K m).
The proposed approach will reduce overall prediction error by roughly 30%.
The intended samples are single-phase HfNbTaTiZr, considered in high-purity and 1 wt.% oxygen-containing variants.
Atomic-scale structural details, anharmonicity, and oxygen-induced defects govern phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Electron-phonon interactions are relevant to heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Machine-learning corrections to DFT-derived properties will capture anharmonic lattice vibrations.
Electronic-structure methods can evaluate the electronic thermal contribution separately from the lattice contribution.
Separating phonon-mediated and electron-mediated transport avoids conflation of the two heat-transport channels.
Lattice conduction dominates in HfNbTaTiZr below 200 K.
Additional impurity phases or significant microstructural defects may reduce the model's accuracy.
The exact error reduction and separation of transport contributions depend on experimental calibration.
The cited PbSnTeSe study combined first-principles DFT, on-the-fly machine learning, semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory, and Green–Kubo theory.
The cited PbSnTeSe study found very low lattice thermal conductivity.
The cited PbSnTeSe study separately evaluated electrical conductivity and electronic thermal conductivity.
A deviation exceeding ±20% between measured and predicted separated conductivities would falsify the proposed accuracy claim.

contradictions.description: The conditions field says lattice conduction dominates below 200 K, whereas the task context says experiments below 200 K indicate that lattice and electronic contributions can be comparable.
